questions.question: Which country took over the presidency of the G7 in January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Canada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Canada assumed the presidency of the G7 in January 2025, taking over from the prior presidency country.
 
• The G7 (Group of Seven) is an intergovernmental organization consisting of the world's largest advanced economies, including the US, UK, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, and Japan.
 
• The presidency of the G7 rotates annually among its member countries, giving each the responsibility of hosting the annual summit and setting the agenda for global discussions.
 
• As the president, Canada is expected to focus on key issues such as climate change, global economic stability, and international security.
 
• The 2025 G7 Summit, under Canada's leadership, will bring together heads of state and government to discuss and coordinate policies on pressing global challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **G7 Overview:**

 
 
• The G7 was established in 1975 as a forum for the world's leading industrialized nations to discuss and coordinate economic policies.
 
• The group addresses global issues such as trade, climate change, development, and security.
 
• Unlike the G20, the G7 does not include emerging economies like China, India, or Brazil.
 
 
 
• **Canada's Role in the G7:**
 
 
• Canada joined the G7 in 1976, one year after its formation, and has hosted the summit several times, most recently in 2018.
 
• The country is known for championing issues like environmental sustainability, gender equality, and global health during its presidencies.
 
 
 
• **Structure of the G7 Presidency:**
 
 
• The presidency is responsible for organizing the annual summit, ministerial meetings, and setting the group’s agenda for the year.
 
• The host country works closely with other member states to ensure consensus on key issues.
 
 
 
• **2025 G7 Agenda:**
 
 
• Although the official agenda is yet to be finalized, Canada is expected to prioritize climate action, energy transition, and global economic recovery.
 
• Other topics may include strengthening global health systems and addressing food security.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements with respect to Dividend Distribution Tax (DDT) in India is/are correct?

 1. DDT was a tax on dividends paid to the shareholders of a company.

 2. Budget 2025-26 has proposed to remove the DDT paid by the companies to investors.

 3. DDT was removed to avoid double taxation of dividends and make the Indian Equity Market more attractive.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dividend Distribution Tax (DDT)** was a tax levied on companies, requiring them to pay a tax on the dividends distributed to shareholders.
 
• The **Finance Act 2020**, not Budget 2025-26, abolished DDT, shifting the tax burden to shareholders who now pay tax on dividends according to their applicable income tax slab.
 
• The removal of DDT was aimed at **avoiding double taxation of dividends**, as earlier companies paid DDT and shareholders also paid taxes on dividends.
 
• This reform was introduced to make the Indian equity market more **investor-friendly** and attract foreign and domestic investments.
 
• DDT was earlier charged at an effective rate of **20.56%** (including surcharge and cess).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **What is Double Taxation?**

 
 
• Double taxation occurs when the same income is taxed twice. Under the old DDT regime, companies paid tax on their profits, and shareholders paid tax on the dividends received.
 
 
 
• **Current Taxation on Dividends:**
 
 
• Post-2020, dividends are taxed in the hands of shareholders based on their applicable income tax slab rates.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs):**
 
 
• The removal of DDT has benefitted FPIs as they can now avail of benefits under tax treaties, reducing their tax burden.
 
 
 
• **Finance Act 2020:**
 
 
• This act introduced key reforms, including the abolition of DDT, to simplify tax structures and boost economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Attractiveness of Equity Markets:**
 
 
• Removing DDT aligns India’s taxation policies with global practices, making Indian equity markets more competitive and attractive to investors.

questions.question: In 2024, India introduced a fast-track procurement clause in which defence procurement policy to reduce acquisition delays?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Defence Acquisition Procedure**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Defence Acquisition Procedure (DAP) 2020 introduced various reforms, including a fast-track procurement clause to address delays in acquiring critical defence equipment.
 
• In 2024, India emphasized this clause to expedite the procurement process for enhancing operational readiness of the armed forces.
 
• Fast-track procurement is aimed at addressing urgent operational requirements during critical situations or emergencies.
 
• The Defence Acquisition Procedure replaced the earlier Defence Procurement Procedure (DPP) and focuses on indigenization under the "Atmanirbhar Bharat" initiative.
 
• The DAP 2020 incorporates numerous measures to promote transparency, efficiency, and accountability in defence acquisitions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Defence Acquisition Procedure (DAP):**

 
 
• It is a comprehensive document that governs the acquisition of defence equipment, systems, and platforms in India.
 
• DAP 2020 emphasizes "Make in India" and self-reliance in the defence sector by encouraging domestic manufacturing.
 
• It classifies procurement into categories such as Buy (Indian-IDDM), Buy (Indian), Buy and Make (Indian), and others to prioritize indigenous production.
 
 
 
• **Fast-Track Procurement:**
 
 
• This mechanism was introduced to meet critical operational needs of the armed forces within a compressed timeline.
 
• It is used in situations of urgency, bypassing lengthy procurement procedures.
 
 
 
• **Indigenization in Defence:**
 
 
• The government aims to achieve self-reliance in defence manufacturing through initiatives like "Atmanirbhar Bharat" and the Strategic Partnership Model.
 
• Efforts are being made to reduce India's reliance on defence imports and promote exports of indigenous defence products.
 
 
 
• **Defence Offset Policy:**
 
 
• This policy mandates foreign vendors to invest a percentage of the contract value in India to develop the domestic defence industry.
 
• It supports technology transfer and collaboration between Indian and foreign defence companies.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the 'Dare Square' Motorcycle Expedition flagged off in January 2025.

 
• The expedition was launched by the Eastern Naval Command as part of INS Ranvijay’s 37th anniversary celebrations.
 
• The rally aims to promote mental health awareness, road safety and maritime heritage among youth through outreach activities.
 
• It was conducted in collaboration with the Indian Air Force and covered northeastern states of India.
 
• The rally culminates at the Dogra Regimental Centre in Ayodhya, highlighting the naval affiliation with the Dogra Regiment.

Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1, 2 and 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 'Dare Square' Motorcycle Expedition was launched by the **Eastern Naval Command** as part of the celebrations for INS Ranvijay’s 37th anniversary.
 
• The primary objectives of the rally included **promoting mental health awareness, road safety, and maritime heritage** among the youth through outreach activities.
 
• The expedition was conducted in collaboration with the Indian Air Force, enhancing inter-service cooperation and synergy.
 
• The rally culminated at the **Dogra Regimental Centre in Ayodhya**, reflecting the naval affiliation with the Dogra Regiment and paying tribute to this association.
 
• Statement 3 is incorrect since the expedition did not specifically cover the northeastern states of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eastern Naval Command (ENC):**

 
 
• Headquartered in Visakhapatnam, the ENC is one of the three operational commands of the Indian Navy.
 
• It plays a critical role in safeguarding India's eastern seaboard and maritime interests in the Bay of Bengal.
 
 
 
• **INS Ranvijay:**
 
 
• INS Ranvijay is a Rajput-class destroyer commissioned into the Indian Navy in 1987.
 
• It is equipped with advanced weaponry and systems, making it a key asset in naval operations.
 
 
 
• **Dogra Regiment:**
 
 
• The Dogra Regiment is one of the oldest infantry regiments of the Indian Army, known for its valor and distinguished service.
 
• The affiliation of naval units with army regiments fosters inter-service camaraderie and mutual respect.
 
 
 
• **Mental Health Awareness in India:**
 
 
• Mental health is a significant concern in India, with initiatives like campaigns and outreach programs aimed at reducing stigma and promoting awareness.
 
• Organizations such as the National Mental Health Programme (NMHP) work to improve mental health services in the country.
 
 
 
• **Road Safety Initiatives:**
 
 
• India has launched programs like the National Road Safety Policy to reduce road accidents and enhance safety awareness.
 
• Public campaigns and enforcement of traffic laws are critical in addressing the high rate of road-related fatalities.

questions.question: Which was the new scheme announced during Budget 2025-26 that targets 100 low productivity districts and focuses on enhancing agricultural productivity, crop diversification, sustainable practices, irrigation and post-harvest storage?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Prime Minister Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana was announced during the Union Budget 2025-26 to address agricultural productivity challenges in 100 low-productivity districts.
 
• The scheme aims to enhance agricultural productivity through crop diversification, sustainable practices, and modern agricultural techniques.
 
• A special focus is placed on improving irrigation infrastructure and ensuring post-harvest storage facilities to minimize crop losses.
 
• The scheme also promotes the adoption of climate-resilient farming practices to ensure long-term sustainability in agricultural activities.
 
• It is designed to uplift farming communities, especially in underdeveloped areas, and contribute to rural economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Crop Diversification:** This refers to the practice of growing a variety of crops to improve soil health, reduce dependency on a single crop, and increase agricultural income.
 
• **Sustainable Agriculture:** It involves farming practices that meet current food needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs, focusing on eco-friendly techniques.
 
• **Irrigation Infrastructure:** Proper irrigation systems help in water management for farming, ensuring that crops receive adequate water during critical growth periods.
 
• **Post-Harvest Management:** This includes activities such as storage, processing, and transportation of crops to prevent spoilage and improve marketability.
 
• **Climate-Resilient Farming:** These are agricultural methods designed to withstand the adverse effects of climate change, such as drought-tolerant crops and water-conservation techniques.

questions.question: Who inaugurated the National Conference on ‘Environment – 2025’ in New Delhi on 29 March 2025?

• As the head of state, Droupadi Murmu has been actively involved in promoting environmental sustainability and climate change awareness.
 
• The event brought together policymakers, environmentalists, scientists, and industry experts to discuss issues such as **climate change mitigation, renewable energy adoption, and biodiversity conservation**.
 
• The conference is considered a significant step towards fulfilling India’s commitment to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: In March 2025, Indian PM Narendra Modi attended the National Day celebrations of which country as the Chief Guest?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended the National Day celebrations of **Mauritius** as the Chief Guest in March 2025.
 
• Mauritius celebrates its National Day on **March 12** every year, marking its independence from British rule in 1968 and its transformation into a Republic in 1992.
 
• PM Modi’s visit highlights the deep-rooted ties between India and Mauritius, which share cultural, historical, and strategic connections.
 
• India has been a key development partner of Mauritius, providing financial and technological assistance in areas like infrastructure, defense, and capacity building.
 
• The visit underscores India’s commitment to its "neighborhood first" and "SAGAR" (Security and Growth for All in the Region) initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• India has supported Mauritius in various sectors, including education, healthcare, and technology.
 
• Key projects like the Metro Express and Supreme Court building in Mauritius were funded by India.
 
 
 
• **SAGAR Initiative:**
 
 
• SAGAR stands for "Security and Growth for All in the Region," an Indian maritime initiative aimed at enhancing security and economic cooperation in the Indian Ocean.
 
• Mauritius is a critical partner under this initiative due to its strategic location in the Indian Ocean.
 
 
 
• **National Day of Mauritius:**
 
 
• The National Day celebrations include parades, cultural events, and speeches commemorating the nation’s achievements.
 
• March 12 is significant as it marks the day of independence and the adoption of the Republican constitution.

• Indo-Mauritian ties date back to the migration of Indian laborers during colonial times, establishing a strong historical bond.
 
• The two countries share a common history of colonial struggles and post-independence development.

questions.question: Which of the following technologies was used to fabricate the Vikram 3201 microprocessor launched in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**180nm CMOS technology**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Vikram 3201 microprocessor, launched in 2025, was fabricated using **180nm CMOS technology**, which is widely regarded as a robust and cost-effective process for microprocessor manufacturing.
 
• **180nm CMOS technology** provides a balanced trade-off between performance, power efficiency, and manufacturing costs, making it ideal for embedded systems and mid-range applications.
 
• This technology has been extensively used in the development of processors, microcontrollers, and SoCs (System on Chips) for consumer electronics and industrial applications.
 
• The Vikram 3201 is expected to play a critical role in advancing India's semiconductor capabilities and reducing dependency on imports.
 
• The development of processors like Vikram 3201 aligns with India’s vision for self-reliance under the "Make in India" initiative, emphasizing indigenous semiconductor manufacturing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **CMOS Technology:** Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor (CMOS) technology is a widely used semiconductor fabrication process known for its low power consumption and high density of integration.
 
• **Semiconductor Nodes:** Semiconductor nodes like 180nm, 90nm, and 7nm define the size of transistors in the chip. Smaller nodes generally offer better performance and efficiency but require advanced manufacturing processes.
 
• **Fabrication Process:** The fabrication process involves designing, layering, and etching silicon wafers to create integrated circuits. 180nm technology represents a mature and reliable node for cost-sensitive applications.
 
• **Indian Semiconductor Mission:** India’s semiconductor mission aims to build a vibrant semiconductor ecosystem and promote R&D, design, and manufacturing within the country.
 
• **Embedded Systems:** Processors like Vikram 3201 are widely used in embedded systems for applications such as IoT devices, automotive control systems, and industrial automation.

questions.question: Which of the following cities is set to host the COP30 climate summit in 2025?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Belem, Brazil**, has been chosen to host the COP30 climate summit in 2025.
 
• The announcement was made by Brazil's President **Luis Inácio Lula da Silva** in 2023.
 
• Belem is located in the Amazon region, highlighting the significance of addressing climate change in one of the world's most critical ecosystems.
 
• The decision aligns with global efforts to focus on **preservation of the Amazon rainforest**, which plays a pivotal role in combating climate change.
 
• COP (Conference of the Parties) is an annual United Nations climate change conference where nations negotiate strategies to address global warming.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **COP Conferences**: These events are part of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), established in 1992 to combat climate change globally.
 
• **Brazil's Environmental Role**: Brazil is home to approximately 60% of the Amazon rainforest, making it a key player in global climate discussions.
 
• **Previous COP Locations**: Recent COP summits include COP26 in Glasgow, UK (2021), and COP27 in Sharm El-Sheikh, Egypt (2022). COP28 is scheduled for Dubai, UAE, in 2023.
 
• **Deforestation Concerns**: The Amazon faces significant threats from deforestation and illegal mining, which contribute to biodiversity loss and increased greenhouse gas emissions.

questions.question: Which global observance did UNESCO mark on 24 January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**International Day of Education**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **International Day of Education** is observed globally on **24 January** every year.
 
• It was proclaimed by the **United Nations General Assembly** in December 2018 to emphasize the role of education in peace and development.
 
• UNESCO leads the global observance of this day, focusing on ensuring inclusive and equitable quality education for all as part of the **Sustainable Development Goal 4** (SDG 4).
 
• The theme for 2025 will highlight the importance of **transformative education** in addressing global challenges such as climate change, inequality, and poverty.
 
• The day serves as a call to action to prioritize education in policy-making and funding globally, aiming to build resilient and sustainable societies.

questions.question: At Aero India 2025, the DRDO unveiled a new technology to enhance aircraft launch capabilities for the Indian Navy. What is this technology called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electro-Magnetic Launch System (EMLS)**__.

__
 
• The Electro-Magnetic Launch System (EMLS) is a cutting-edge technology unveiled by the DRDO for the Indian Navy to enhance aircraft launch capabilities.
 
• EMLS employs electromagnetic force to launch aircraft from naval carriers, replacing conventional steam catapults.
 
• This technology provides greater efficiency, precision, and flexibility in launching heavier and advanced aircraft.
 
• EMLS is aligned with India's efforts to modernize naval aviation and boost indigenous defense capabilities under the "Atmanirbhar Bharat" initiative.
 
• It is a critical component for operating advanced fighters and unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) from aircraft carriers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electromagnetic Aircraft Launch System (EMALS):**

 
 
• EMALS, developed by the US Navy, is a similar system that uses electromagnetic energy to launch aircraft.
 
• It offers a smoother acceleration compared to steam catapults, reducing wear and tear on aircraft.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of EMLS:**
 
 
• Improved energy efficiency and reduced maintenance costs compared to steam-based systems.
 
• Capable of launching a wide range of aircraft, from lightweight UAVs to heavy fighter jets.
 
• Provides scalability and adaptability for future advanced aircraft designs.
 
 
 
• **Indian Navy's Aircraft Carriers:**
 
 
• India currently operates INS Vikramaditya and recently commissioned INS Vikrant, both of which will benefit from advanced launch systems like EMLS.
 
 
 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat in Defense:**
 
 
• The DRDO's development of EMLS reflects India's commitment to self-reliance in defense technologies.

• Drone surveying ensures **high-resolution aerial imagery** that facilitates precision mapping and minimizes disputes related to land ownership.
 
• The maps generated via drones are integrated with **Geographical Information Systems (GIS)** for ease of access and management.
 
• This initiative aims to promote **financial stability in rural areas** by enabling landowners to use their property as collateral for loans and other financial activities.

• **Objectives of SVAMITVA Scheme**:

questions.question: How many religious communities are covered under the 2019 Citizenship Amendment Act?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4 (6 religious communities)**__.

• The Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) 2019 covers **6 religious communities:** Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, and Christians.
 
• The act aims to provide Indian citizenship to persecuted religious minorities from **Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Afghanistan** who entered India on or before **31 December 2014**.
 
• It applies to individuals who faced religious persecution in these countries and were forced to migrate to India.
 
• The CAA **excludes Muslims** from its purview, as it focuses on non-Muslim minorities.
 
• The law does not alter the existing process of acquiring citizenship for others but facilitates faster citizenship for persecuted minorities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of Citizenship:** Citizenship refers to the legal status granted to an individual by a country, entitling them to certain rights and responsibilities.
 
• **Religious Persecution:** It refers to systematic mistreatment or oppression based on religious beliefs, often forcing affected individuals to flee their country.
 
• **Countries Covered:** The CAA specifically applies to refugees from **Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Afghanistan**, which are predominantly Muslim-majority nations.
 
• **Criticism of CAA:** Critics argue that the act violates the secular fabric of the Indian Constitution by excluding Muslims and raises concerns about discrimination.
 
• **NRC Connection:** The CAA has been linked to the proposed National Register of Citizens (NRC), which aims to identify illegal immigrants. However, the relationship between the two remains a contentious issue.

questions.question: What is the NISAR satellite, launched in February 2025 and co-developed by ISRO and NASA, designed for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Earth observation and climate monitoring**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **NISAR** (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) is a joint Earth observation satellite developed collaboratively by NASA and ISRO.
 
• The satellite is designed to monitor **ecosystem disturbances, natural hazards, and global environmental changes** such as ice sheet dynamics, forest biomass, and agricultural patterns.
 
• Equipped with **dual-frequency radar systems (L-band by NASA and S-band by ISRO)**, NISAR ensures high-resolution imaging capabilities.
 
• The mission aims to deliver critical data for **climate monitoring, disaster management**, and resource mapping globally.
 
• It is set to launch in **February 2025**, marking a significant collaboration in Earth science between the two space agencies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR):**

 
 
• A radar technology that creates high-resolution images of the Earth's surface by emitting and receiving microwave signals.
 
• It is capable of penetrating clouds, vegetation, and even soil, making it useful for all-weather, day-night observations.
 
 
 
• **L-band and S-band Radars:**
 
 
• L-band radar (long wavelength) is ideal for monitoring vegetation and soil moisture, while S-band radar (shorter wavelength) is suited for detecting finer details like ice and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Key Applications of NISAR:**
 
 
• Tracking deforestation, agricultural patterns, and glacier movements.
 
• Monitoring natural disasters like earthquakes, tsunamis, and floods to aid in disaster response.
 
 
 
• **Data Contribution:**
 
 
• NISAR will provide up to 12 terabytes of imaging data daily, supporting global climate studies and environmental monitoring.
 
 
 
• **ISRO-NASA Collaboration:**
 
 
• This partnership strengthens international cooperation in space exploration and enhances the technological capabilities of both agencies.

questions.question: Which of the following changes was introduced in 2024 under the Companies Act amendments to enhance corporate social responsibility (CSR) transparency in India?

options.text: Exemption of companies with a turnover below ₹500 crore from CSR obligations
Reduction in the minimum CSR spending threshold for all eligible companies
Requirement for at least 50% of board members to be CSR specialists
Mandatory quarterly CSR reporting accompanied by independent audits

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mandatory quarterly CSR reporting accompanied by independent audits**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In 2024, the Indian government amended the Companies Act to improve **Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) transparency**.
 
• The amendment introduced **mandatory quarterly CSR reporting** for eligible companies to ensure regular updates on CSR activities.
 
• Independent audits of the CSR reports were made **compulsory** to enhance credibility and accountability.
 
• The change aims to address issues of non-compliance, misuse of CSR funds, and ensure alignment of CSR activities with their intended social objectives.
 
• This step is part of broader efforts to encourage **responsible corporate governance** and increase trust among stakeholders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR):**

 
 
• CSR refers to the practices where businesses voluntarily contribute to sustainable development by delivering economic, social, and environmental benefits.
 
• In India, Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 mandates CSR spending for companies meeting certain financial thresholds.
 
• Eligible companies must spend at least 2% of their average net profit of the last 3 years on CSR activities.
 
 
 
• **Independent Audits:**
 
 
• Independent audits involve third-party examination of financial or operational processes to ensure compliance and accuracy.
 
• In the context of CSR, these audits validate the effectiveness and alignment of CSR projects with prescribed norms.
 
 
 
• **CSR Reporting:**
 
 
• CSR reporting involves documenting and disclosing information about a company’s CSR activities, expenditures, and outcomes.
 
• Quarterly reporting ensures transparency and provides regular updates to stakeholders about the company’s contribution to social development.
 
 
 
• **Impact of CSR Amendments:**
 
 
• Improves corporate accountability and stakeholder confidence.
 
• Encourages companies to align their CSR initiatives with national development goals.
 
• Addresses misuse or underutilization of CSR funds by ensuring stricter compliance.

questions.question: According to the NITI Aayog's policy brief 'India’s Booming Gig and Platform Economy' (2022), what is the projected size of the gig workforce in India by 2029-30?

• As of 2020-21, the gig workforce in India was estimated at about **7.7 million**, indicating a significant growth trajectory in the coming years.
 
• The report highlights that gig workers currently constitute approximately **1.5% of India's total workforce**, with this share expected to rise to 4.1% by 2029-30.

• **Gig Economy:**

 
 
• The gig economy refers to a labor market characterized by the prevalence of short-term contracts or freelance work as opposed to permanent jobs.
 
• Examples include ride-sharing drivers (e.g., Uber, Ola), food delivery workers (e.g., Swiggy, Zomato), and freelance professionals in areas such as IT and creative industries.
 
 
 
• **Platform Economy:**
 
 
• The platform economy is driven by digital platforms that connect service providers with consumers, such as e-commerce platforms, ride-hailing apps, and freelance marketplaces.
 
• It plays a pivotal role in enabling the gig economy by facilitating access to work opportunities.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog's Recommendations:**
 
 
• The report emphasizes the need for **social security measures** for gig workers, including health insurance, skill development, and worker protections.
 
• It also advocates for the **formalization of gig work** through regulatory frameworks to ensure fair labor practices.
 
 
 
• **Key Sectors in the Gig Economy:**
 
 
• Prominent sectors include transportation, logistics, e-commerce, healthcare, and personal services.
 
• The demand for gig workers is expected to grow across both urban and rural areas, with a focus on last-mile delivery and service accessibility.
 
 
 
• **Challenges Faced by Gig Workers:**
 
 
• Gig workers often face **income instability, lack of social security benefits, and limited career progression opportunities**.
 
• Addressing these issues through policy interventions is crucial for sustaining the growth of the gig economy.

• Various campaigns and events are organized across the country to spread awareness about the importance of saving, educating, and empowering the girl child.
 
• The celebration aligns with the goals of government schemes like **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao**, which focuses on improving the welfare and status of girls in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP):**

 
 
• Launched in 2015, it aims to address declining **Child Sex Ratio (CSR)** and promote the survival, protection, and education of the girl child.
 
• The campaign is a tri-ministerial effort involving the Ministries of Women and Child Development, Health and Family Welfare, and Education.
 
 
 
• **Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY):**
 
 
• A government-backed savings scheme aimed at securing the future of girl children.
 
• Parents can open an account for a girl child below 10 years, with benefits like tax exemptions and high-interest rates.
 
 
 
• **Gender Inequality in India:**
 
 
• India has faced challenges like **female infanticide, child marriage, and gender-based violence**, which these initiatives aim to address.
 
• Promoting girl child education and empowerment is pivotal to achieving societal progress and economic development.
 
 
 
• **United Nations International Day of the Girl Child:**
 
 
• Celebrated globally on **11th October**, it complements India's National Girl Child Day by advocating for girls' rights worldwide.
 
• The focus is on issues like education, healthcare access, and ending child marriage.

questions.question: In January 2025, National Youth Day was celebrated to mark the birth anniversary of which Indian leader?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swami Vivekananda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• National Youth Day is celebrated annually on **12th January** to commemorate the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda.
 
• The Government of India declared Swami Vivekananda's birthday as National Youth Day in **1984** to honor his contributions towards inspiring youth.
 
• Swami Vivekananda, a key figure in introducing Indian philosophies like Vedanta and Yoga to the Western world, believed in the power of youth for nation-building.
 
• His teachings focused on **self-confidence, self-reliance, and spirituality**, making him an ideal role model for Indian youth.
 
• Various programs, including speeches, seminars, cultural performances, and competitions, are organized across India on National Youth Day to spread awareness about his life and ideals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swami Vivekananda:**

 
 
• Born on **12th January 1863** in Kolkata, India, he was originally named Narendranath Datta.
 
• He was a disciple of **Ramakrishna Paramahamsa** and went on to establish the **Ramakrishna Mission** in 1897.
 
• Swami Vivekananda is best known for his speech at the **1893 Parliament of the World's Religions** in Chicago, where he introduced Hinduism to the global audience.
 
• His famous quote, "Arise, awake, and stop not till the goal is reached," continues to inspire millions worldwide.
 
 
 
• **National Youth Day Themes:**
 
 
• Every year, National Youth Day is celebrated with a particular theme to engage the youth in constructive activities.
 
• The themes are centered around topics like **youth empowerment, innovation, and spirituality**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of National Youth Day:**
 
 
• The day serves to highlight the role of youth in shaping the future of the nation.
 
• It encourages young people to imbibe the teachings of Swami Vivekananda and work towards self-development and societal progress.
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition:**
 
 
• Swami Vivekananda's ideas on religious harmony, universal brotherhood, and the empowerment of youth resonate globally.
 
• His contributions to philosophy and spirituality have earned him recognition as one of India's greatest cultural ambassadors.
